serves_registry_rows: persons per household (the size distribution of households, by density class of the census unit, by tenure and by structure band)

sources.name: American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table-based summary file: B25008, B25009, B25032, B25033, B26001, at census tract and block group; 2024 tract gazetteer; 2024 cartographic boundary file for block groups (land area only)
sources.licence: no licence text attached; the Bureau asks to be cited as the source
sources.notice: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-Year Estimates, Tables B25008, B25009, B25032, B25033 and B26001. This table is a derived work; it is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau. (The conventional source line; the Bureau's citation page was not re-read for this build.)

keys.unit: census tract, and separately block group, of the 50 states and DC; Puerto Rico not read
keys.class: 1 village, 2 suburban, 3 terraced, 4 apartment blocks, 5 dense fabric: lower bounds 0, 250, 1500, 6000, 12000 people in households per km2 of the UNIT's own land area; units under 1 per km2 not read (twin/globe classes.json)

envelope.population: households only; group quarters (2.4 % of people) are outside it
envelope.key: density of a census unit, not of a 1 km tile and not of a twin leaf; the two census keys agree within both budgets in the three resolved classes
envelope.classes_resolved: village, suburban, terraced by county count; apartment blocks and dense fabric are unresolved (effective counties 17 and 8) and their rows are readings only

budgets.whose: the campaign author's, on the consumer's behalf, stated before any file was read

law: each row's seven shares sum to 1,000,000 within 4 parts (rounding); persons_per_household is the published household population over households and is NOT the mean of the banded shares (the open top band's residual mean is about 12, not 8)
checker: python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('household_table.json'));assert all(abs(sum(r['shares_ppm'])-10**6)<=4 for k in d['keys'].values() for r in k['rows'].values())"

verdict.generator: TWIN-SIZE-0: the twin's own emitted histogram, twin/hhsize b939214, sha256 438568abd0258d56bad0d2e286c98e3e03d855848969465af79914971bb0a418
verdict.households_per_leaf: certified nationally and in village and suburban; unresolved in terraced (the reference's own split-half gap, 0.10, exceeds half the budget) and in the two densest classes
verdict.household_composition: refused nationally (one-person share 0.182 against 0.286) and in village and suburban; unresolved in terraced by the frozen error floor although the miss (0.117) is five times that gap; unresolved in the two densest classes
verdict.for_the_twins_own_leaves: outside the envelope: a leaf has no census unit. The verdicts are about the rule as a description of US households pooled by census-unit density.

limits: density class is a weak key: a rule keyed by class puts 18.3 % of large county-classes' households within both budgets, one national rule 17.2 %
structure band and tenure are strong keys and are published as readings with no verdict
one-person share by structure band does not exist in these tables (two margins, no joint)
the window includes 2020, collected at about two thirds of the usual responses
2.0 % of households sit in excluded units (heavy group quarters, no land, under the floor)
holds_no_real_feature: This table holds no coordinate, id, name or tag of any real feature, tract, block group, county or state. It holds rows of counts and shares by class.
